masking.py:157-167 selects positions via enumerate(df.columns), copies the frame, calls masked.isetitem(i, Series) per position, then sets masked.attrs = dict(df.attrs). pandas is pinned at 3.1.0 (requirements.txt:79) and pyproject allows >=2.0,<4. DataFrame.isetitem (added in pandas 1.5) sets the column by integer position, not label, so duplicate labels are handled. The Series is built with index=df.index, so no reindex happens even with duplicate index values. DataFrame.attrs has a documented setter that takes a dict. Both usages are supported in every allowed pandas version. This rests on my knowledge of the pandas API; I did not run the code or read the pandas source.

criteria.json read, criterion 3 present and the file is well-formed, so it counts. Traced each label through split_label_words/_split_chunk/_word_matches/_label_matches in masking.py:63-124 against BUILTIN_SECRET_ENTRIES (28-60). Masked: password_hash -> [password,hash]; PasswordHash -> U'P'+L'assword' -> 'Password','Hash'; session_token -> token; recovery_hash -> hash; pin; PINs -> U'PIN'+L's' with no following run -> word 'pins' = pin+'s'; APIKey -> 'API','Key' matches entry 'api key'; api_keys -> api,keys (keys = key+s) matches 'api key'; OTPSecret -> 'OTP','Secret' matches otp; password2 -> digits split off, 'password'; users.password_hash -> '.' is a separator, hash; access_key, encryption_key, verification_code, one_time_code match the multi-word entries. Not masked: id, name, email, phone, last_login_ip (last,login,ip), session_expires (no 'session key'), Key (no single-word 'key' entry), COLUMN_KEY (column,key), sort_key, zip_code (no bare 'code' entry), author_id (author is not auth, no match) all match no entry.
